SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abu Jahl came upon the Prophet praying and forbade him, prompting the passage about the one who forbids a servant when he prays through the sinful, lying forelock.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r3.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي فجاءه أبو جهل فنهاه فأنزل الله ﴿ أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى ﴾

BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r10.claim: The second conditional means that the forbidding man lies against the truth and turns from right guidance; its answer is the question whether he knows God sees.
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r10.anchor: {أرءيت} أخبرني ذلك الناهي {إن كذب وتولى} أي إن

BURSEVI:v10p366/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366/r13.claim: The second condition stands separately to signal that denial and turning away occur independently and bring the threat; the first supposition is impossible and merely broadens the comparison.
BURSEVI:v10p366/r13.anchor: فأمر مستحيل قد ذكر في حيز الشرط لتوسيع الدائرة وهو السر في تجريد الشرطية الأولى

BURSEVI:v10p366/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366/r14.claim: An alternative reading asks whether the worshipper is guided and commands piety while the forbidding man is a denier who turns away—an astonishing contrast.
BURSEVI:v10p366/r14.anchor: وقيل : العنى أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا يصلي والمنهي على الهدى

QASHANI:96:9-14/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:96:9-14/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:96:9-14/r3.claim: If the arrogant man denied truth and turned from the straight religion in stubbornness, he should know God sees either state and will requite him.
QASHANI:96:9-14/r3.anchor: بالحق لكفره وأعرض عن الدين المستقيم لعناده وطغيانه

QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r14.claim: The warning that God sees is a call to vigilance; one who has not attained vigilance cannot advance to direct witnessing.
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r14.anchor: ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى } . أي : ما الذي يستحقه من هذه صفته ؟ والتخويف برؤية

TUSTARI:96:14/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:96:14/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:96:14/r1.claim: Nothing lies behind God, while He is behind every beyond.
TUSTARI:96:14/r1.anchor: قال: ليس له وراء، وهو وراء كل وراء.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r2.claim: “Have you seen” expresses amazement at a known extraordinary event; seeing is intellectual, its second object is omitted and supplied by the final question in verse 14.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r2.anchor: تقال للذي يعلم أنه رأى حالا عجيبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r3.claim: The interrogative conveys astonishment through a rhetorical transfer: people ask for confirmation of something so extraordinary that it is hard to believe.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r3.anchor: فاستعمال الاستفهام في التعجيب مجاز مرسل في التركيب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r3.claim: The vision verb is intellectual, with both objects omitted for concision; the previous servant identifies the first, and the previous prohibition supplies the second.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r3.anchor: وحذف مفعولا فعل الرؤية اختصارا لدلالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r8.claim: The clause begins a fresh threat: if the man denies the call and turns away, should he think God does not know what he does? The first object of “have you seen” is omitted and refers to the forbidding man.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r8.anchor: جملة مستأنفة للتهديد والوعيد على التكذيب والتولي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes the question in verse 14 as the answer to the condition; al-Radi allows an interrogative answer without the expected fa, comparing another conditional question.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r9.anchor: ولم يعتبر وجوب اقتران جملة جواب الشرط بالفاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r10.claim: Most grammarians, including al-Zamakhshari in al-Mufassal, require the fa; on their analysis the implicit answer is that God knows and will punish him, and verse 14 independently denies the offender’s ignorance.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r1.claim: Saying God sees him is an indirect threat of punishment; “knows” includes certainty, and the interrogative rebukes him for failing to know and protect himself from punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r1.anchor: وكني بأن الله يرى عن الوعيد بالعقاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r2.claim: The verb “know” carries the sense of certainty, which accounts for its construction with “bi”.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r3.claim: The question suspends the verb “have you seen” from taking its object because an interrogative follows.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r4.claim: The conditional predicts that Abu Jahl will deny the Prophet when called to Islam and turn away; God promises to give the Prophet justice against him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r4.anchor: بأن أبا جهل سيكذبه حين يدعوه إلى الإسلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r5.claim: The denial’s pronoun refers to the man who forbids prayer, while the object of “deny” is omitted because the preceding context identifies the servant he denies.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r5.anchor: وحذف مفعول { كذب } لدلالة ما قبله عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r6.claim: The object of God’s seeing is omitted to make the statement encompass every existent; divine seeing means knowledge of perceptible things.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r6.anchor: والمراد بالرؤية المسندة إلى الله تعالى تعلق علمه بالمحسوسات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r6.claim: God's seeing means perceiving everyone's deeds; the wording does not imply a bodily organ or likeness to created things.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r6.anchor: ونسب الرؤية إلى الله تعالى بمعنى يدرك أعمال الجميع بإدراك: سماه رؤية، والله منزه عن الجارحة

AKHFASH:v2p582/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p582/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p582/r1.claim: The second arāʾayta clause in verse 13 is appositional to the first in verse 11, and the predicate is the statement in verse 14 that God sees.
AKHFASH:v2p582/r1.anchor: وجعل الخبر {ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى}

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#3/r1.claim: The verse refers to Abu Jahl: God sees his conduct and will requite him for it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#3/r1.anchor: يعني أبا جهل بأن الله يرى ذلك فيجازيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r5.claim: God asks whether the forbidding opponent realizes that God sees and hears him, and will repay him fully for what he does.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r5.anchor: أي: أما علم هذا الناهي لهذا المهتدي أن الله يراه ويسمع كلامه، وسيجازيه على فعله أتم الجزاء.

FARRA:v3p278/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p278/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p278/r7.claim: “Does he not know that God sees?” refers to Abū Jahl.
FARRA:v3p278/r7.anchor:
الله يرى (14) .
يعني: أبا جهل، ثم قال: «كلا لئن لم ينته

JISHUMI:v10p7481/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r13.claim: Knowing that God sees one's deeds should deter sin because He will hold the denier accountable.
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r13.anchor: يرى ما يأتيه هذا المكذب، فيعلم أنه يؤاخذه به، أشار إلى أن علم الإنسان بأن الله يرى

JISHUMI:v10p7482/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r7.claim: God literally sees things; the author says this is possible and rejects the Baghdādī claim that “sees” means “knows.”
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r7.anchor: ويدل قوله: (ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى) أنه يرى الأشياء، وحقيقته جائز، فلا معنى للعدول

KASHSHAF:96:14/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:14/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:14/r1.claim: God sees a person's guidance or error and will recompense him accordingly; this is a threat.
KASHSHAF:96:14/r1.anchor: ويطلع على أحواله من هداه وضلاله فيجازيه على حسب ذلك

KASHSHAF:96:14/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:14/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:14/r2.claim: The objects of arayta are the one who forbids and the conditional clause together.
KASHSHAF:96:14/r2.anchor: الذي ينهى مع الجملة الشرطية ،   وهما في موضع المفعولين

KASHSHAF:96:14/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:14/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:14/r3.claim: The first conditional's answer is omitted: if he is guided or commands piety, does he not know God sees? The answer is supplied by the second condition.
KASHSHAF:96:14/r3.anchor: هو محذوف ،   تقديره : إن كان على الهدى أو أمر بالتقوى

KASHSHAF:96:14/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:14/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:14/r4.claim: A question can validly serve as the answer to a condition, as the examples demonstrate.
KASHSHAF:96:14/r4.anchor: كما صحّ في قولك : إن أكرمتك أتكرمني

KASHSHAF:96:14/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:14/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:14/r5.claim: The second arayta between the objects repeats the expression for emphasis.

KASHSHAF:96:14/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:14/r6.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF:96:14/r6.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the person as Umayya ibn Khalaf, who stopped Salman from praying.
KASHSHAF:96:14/r6.anchor: وعن الحسن أنه أمية بن خلف كان ينهى سلمان عن الصلاة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r8.claim: The question may ask Muhammad whether he knows that God sees Abu Jahl, or ask Abu Jahl whether he knows God sees him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r8.anchor: ألم تعلم يا محمد أن الله يرى أبا جهل ؟ الثاني : ألم تعلم يا أبا جهل أن الله يراك ؟

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r9.claim: God sees Abu Jahl's deeds and hears his words.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r9.anchor: أحدهما : يرى عمله ويسمع قوله . الثاني : يراك

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r10.claim: Alternatively, God sees Abu Jahl while he is praying and being forbidden by Abu Jahl.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r10.anchor: الثاني : يراك في صلاتك حين نهاك أبو جهل عنها . ويحتمل ثالثا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r11.claim: A further possibility is that God sees what Abu Jahl intended and will not let him harm His Messenger.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r11.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثا : يرى ما هم به أبو جهل فلا يمكنه من رسوله .

MUQATIL:96:9-19/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r3.claim: The denier who turns away is Abū Jahl, who rejects the Qur'an; God sees both the Prophet alone and Abū Jahl's assembled company.
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r3.anchor: يعني وأعرض { ألم يعلم } أبو جهل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#8/r1.claim: God sees and knows the forbiddener's guidance or error and will repay him accordingly; the first rhetorical question and conditional clauses serve as the two objects of “Have you seen?”, with the conditional answer elided and the second question repeated for emphasis.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#8/r1.anchor: ويطلع على أحواله من هداه وضلاله فيجازيه على حسب حاله وهذا وعيد

NAHHAS:v5p261/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p261/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p261/r15.claim: God sees and knows his action and will punish him for it.
NAHHAS:v5p261/r15.anchor: أي يراه ويعلم فعله فيعاقبه عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:96:13-14/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:13-14/r2.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:96:13-14/r2.claim: Al-Farra reads the three conditional questions together: the servant is guided and commands piety while the forbidding man denies and turns away, making his behavior astonishing; the question about God's seeing him confirms and rebukes, and each later ar'ayta may stand in place of the first.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:13-14/r2.anchor: وقال الفراء: المعنى { أرأيت الذي ينهى * عبدا إذا صلى } وهو على الهدى،

QURTUBI-FULL:96:13-14/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:13-14/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:13-14/r3.claim: God sees Abu Jahl and knows his conduct; the question is a confirmation and rebuke, and the statement about God's seeing is the answer.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:13-14/r3.anchor: ألم يعلم أبو جهل بأن الله يرى أي يراه ويعلم فعله فهو تقرير وتوبيخ

QUTB-ZILAL:96:14/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:14/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:14/r1.claim: God sees the opponent's denial and turning away and his attempt to stop a believing worshiper who is guided and urges piety; this is an implicit threat.

RAZI:96:14/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:14/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:96:14/r1.claim: The verse threatens resurrection and full recompense: God knows everything and neglects nothing, so every person will receive complete requital; it warns sinners and encourages the obedient.
RAZI:96:14/r1.anchor: المقصود من الآية التهديد بالحشر والنشر ، والمعنى أنه تعالى عالم بجميع المعلومات

RAZI:96:14/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:14/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:96:14/r2.claim: Although revealed about Abū Jahl, anyone who prevents obedience to God shares his threat; restrictions in a usurped house or disliked prayer times target sin, as do a master’s or husband’s limits on voluntary worship to preserve welfare with God’s permission.
RAZI:96:14/r2.anchor: كل من نهى من طاعة الله فهو شريك أبي جهل في هذا الوعيد

RAZI-FULL:v32p22#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p22#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p22#3/r1.claim: The verse threatens resurrection and complete requital: God knows everything, is wise, and nothing as small as an atom escapes Him, so He will fully repay each person, frightening sinners and encouraging the obedient.
RAZI-FULL:v32p22#3/r1.anchor: المقصود من الآية التهديد بالحشر والنشر

RAZI-FULL:v32p22#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p22#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p22#3/r2.claim: Although revealed about Abu Jahl, everyone who prevents obedience to God shares his warning.
RAZI-FULL:v32p22#3/r2.anchor: وإن نزلت في حق أبي جهل فكل من نهى من طاعة الله فهو شريك أبي جهل

RAZI-FULL:v32p22#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p22#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p22#3/r3.claim: The threat does not condemn forbidding prayer in a usurped house or disliked times: what is forbidden is the accompanying transgression, not prayer itself.
RAZI-FULL:v32p22#3/r3.anchor: لأن المنهى عنه غير الصلاة وهو المعصية

RAZI-FULL:v32p22#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p22#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p22#3/r4.claim: A master may prevent a slave's night prayer or voluntary fast, and a husband his wife's retreat, to secure her interest with her Lord's permission, not out of hostility to worship.
RAZI-FULL:v32p22#3/r4.anchor: لأن ذلك لاستيفاء مصلحته بإذن ربه لا بغضا لعبادة ربه

TAB:96:14/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:14/r1.speaker: author
TAB:96:14/r1.claim: Abu Jahl should know that God sees him forbidding Muhammad's worship and prayer, and should fear God's might and punishment.
TAB:96:14/r1.anchor: ألم يعلم أبو جهل إذ ينهى محمدا عن عبادة ربه ،   والصلاة له ،   بأن الله يراه فيخاف سطوته وعقابه

TAB:96:14/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:14/r2.speaker: author
TAB:96:14/r2.claim: The three repetitions of araʾayta work by substitution; the sense is whether the forbidding, denying man knows that God sees him.
TAB:96:14/r2.anchor: أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى ،   أرأيت إن كان على الهدى } ،   فكررت أرأيت مرات ثلاثا على البدل

TABATABAI:96:11-19/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r3.claim: Knowing that God sees follows by implication from belief that He created everything and therefore knows and can do everything; polytheists acknowledged these divine attributes despite their negligence.
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r3.anchor: لازم الاعتقاد بأن الله خالق كل شيء هو الاعتقاد بأن له علما بكل شيء

TABRISI:96:9-15/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:9-15/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:9-15/r7.claim: God sees his actions and knows what he does; the implied question asks what punishment this behavior deserves. The verse also signals that one must obey and leave sin.
TABRISI:96:9-15/r7.anchor: ما يفعله ويعلم ما يصنعه والتقدير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176/r1.claim: The one being admonished is the forbiddener, Abū Jahl; God sees his act and will requite him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p176/r1.anchor: {ألم يعلم} الناهي: أبا جهل. {بأن الله يرى} أي انه يرى ذلك فيجازيه

WAHIDI-QT:96:14/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:96:14/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:96:14/r1.claim: Abu Jahl should know that God sees him and knows what he does.
WAHIDI-QT:96:14/r1.anchor: { ألم يعلم } أبو جهل { بأن الله يرى } أي يراه ويعلم ما يفعله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r6.claim: Abu Jahl should know that God sees him and knows what he does.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r6.anchor: ألم يعلم } أبو جهل { بأن الله يرى } أي: يراه ويعلم ما يفعله.

ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r15.claim: God sees right and wrong, good and evil, and will repay everyone according to their deeds.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r15.anchor: Sonra kendisine varılacak olan Allah her hâlde doğruyu da eğriyi de, iyiyi de kötüyü de hepsini görür ve herkesin ameline göre cezâsını verir

ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r16.claim: The pronoun in “does he not know” can refer to either interlocutor: the servant knows God sees all and will not obey, or the prohibitor is asked whether he still fails to know; both readings threaten him.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r16.anchor: Hitab nâhiye olduğu surette “abd”e râci‘olup istifhâm-ı inkârî olarak: “O kul Allah’ın hepsini gördüğünü bilir. Senin nehyini dinlemez ey azgın!” demek olur

ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r17.speaker: Keşşâf
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r17.claim: Al-Kashshaf allows both conditional clauses to have expressed consequences, but the author prefers treating them as omitted and the following statement as an independent resumption.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r17.anchor: Keşşâf’ın dediği gibi iki şartın ikisinin de cevâbı yapmak câiz olsa bile şartların cezâları mahzuf olarak bunun bir cümle-i istînâfiye olması daha muvâfıktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:9/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:9/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:9/r2.claim: A universal reading is more suitable: all tyrants in every age who obstruct religion's work of shaping social life by goodness, truth, and justice are criticized.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:9/r2.anchor: her dönemde görülen ve dinin sosyal hayatı iyilik, hak ve adalet ilkeleri yönünde şekillendirme işlevini engellemek isteyen bütün zorbaların eleştirildiği

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:14:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:14:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:14:anmerkung/r1.claim: The divine name Allah is treated in the note to 95:8.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:14:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zum Gottesnamen Allāh vgl. die Anmerkung zu 95:8

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p390/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p390/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p390/r2.claim: The offender should realize that God sees his unrestrained conduct and will justly avenge preventing His servants from worshipping Him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p390/r2.anchor: the Almighty is watching all his unrestrained behaviour

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p509/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p509/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p509/r9.claim: God sees the forbidd er's guidance or error and will recompense him accordingly; this is a threat.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p509/r9.anchor: ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى، ويطلع على أحواله من هداه وضلاله، فيجازيه على حسب ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p509/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p509/r13.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p509/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the final question completes the rebuke and threat for each of the three preceding conditional constructions, compressing their implied conclusions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p509/r13.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى: إكمال التوبيخ والوعيد بحسب التوفيقات الثلاثة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#3/r1.claim: The missing objects and conditional answers are supplied in several ways: the answers may be omitted as understood from alam yaʿlam, or the result may be anticipated by raʾayta; the passage also follows a semantic request pattern, not grammatical coordination.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#3/r1.anchor: وجواب الشرط في الجملتين محذوف لدلالة ألم يعلم عليه ويقدر حسبما تقتضيه الصناعة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#3/r2.claim: Raʾayta means tell me: since seeing leads to knowledge, asking to see something functions as asking to be informed about it; grammarians differ whether this applies to visual and mental seeing alike.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#3/r2.anchor: فإن الرؤية لما كانت سببا للعلم أجرى الأستفهام عنها مجرى الأستخبار عن متعلقها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#3/r3.claim: Most take the address throughout as any capable listener; another view addresses humankind as in 96:8. The indefinite ʿabdan can signal that the prohibition occurred during prayer, and separated clauses emphasize each warning independently.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#3/r3.anchor: والخطاب في الكل على ما اختاره جمع لكل من يصلح أن يكون مخاطبا ممن له مسكة وقيل للإنسان كالخطاب في إلى ربك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#3/r4.claim: The passage escalates its rebuke in three stages: forbidding prayer outright; forbidding it even if the man claims to be guided or to command piety; and forbidding it while he actually rejects and turns away from the truth.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#3/r4.anchor: وهذا كالترقي في التشنيع والجمهور على عدم تقييد ما في حيز الشرطيتين بما ذكرنا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#3/r5.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#3/r5.claim: The majority read both conditions without al-Alusi's constraints: the man might claim a sound way in what he forbids or enjoin piety by calling to idols, while in reality rejecting truth and turning away.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#3/r5.anchor: الجمهور على عدم تقييد ما في حيز الشرطيتين بما ذكرنا حيث قالوا إن كان على طريقة سديدة فيما ينهى عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#3/r6.claim: Another parsing makes the first raʾayta visual, while the second and third are mental; the last conditional with its explicit answer fills the second object, while the preceding answer is omitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#3/r6.anchor: وقيل إن الرؤية في الجملة الأولى بصرية فلا تحتاج إلى مفعول ثان وفي الثانية والثالثة قلبية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p184/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p184/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p184/r1.claim: A further parse takes all three raʾaytas as mental: the first two have conditional clauses as their second objects, the second repeats the first, and the third is independent by contrast with the opposing conditions.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p184/r1.anchor: وقيل أن أرأيت في الجمل الثلاث من الرؤية القلبية والمفعول الأول للأولى الموصول

ALUSI-FULL:v30p184/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p184/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p184/r2.claim: Leaving the final clause unjoined sharpens the rebuke and asserts the real condition; stating its answer makes it an explicit threat, while earlier conditions merely widen the hypothetical field.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p184/r2.anchor: وفي الإتيان بالجملة الأخيرة من دون العطف ترشيح للكلام المبكت وتنبيه على حقية الشرط

ALUSI-FULL:v30p184/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p184/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p184/r3.claim: The challenge is framed as fair-minded concession: it says ʿabdan rather than chosen prophet and asks any discerning hearer to consider the forbidding man even if he claimed guidance and piety.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p184/r3.anchor: والكلام من قبيل الكلام المنصف وإرخاء العنان ولذا قيل عبدا ولم يقل نبيا مجتبى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p184/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p184/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p184/r4.claim: The implied warning asks whether the forbidding man knows God sees his acts and will repay him, after rebuking him both for missing the guided course and for earning punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p184/r4.anchor: ألم يعلم أن الله يرى ويطلع على أحواله فيجازيه بها حتى اجترأ على ما فعل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r1.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r1.claim: Abū Ḥayyān and others object that a conditional cannot be the second object of raʾayta, which must be an interrogative or oath clause; al-Khafājī later offers a semantic defense.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r1.anchor: واعترض أيضا جعل الجملة الشرطية في موضع المفعول الثاني لا رأيت بأن مفعولها الثاني لا يكون إلا جملة استفهامية كما نص عليه أبو حيان

ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r2.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r2.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says no grammarian he knows permits an interrogative clause to answer a conditional without fa, except in poetic necessity.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r2.anchor: وقال أبو حيان إن وقوع جملة الإستفهام جوابا للشرط بغير فاء لا أعلم أحد أجازه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r3.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r3.claim: Al-Khafājī defends treating the conditional as the second object: the conditional and interrogative answer jointly fill the position through their semantic indication; al-Raḍī and al-Damāmīnī also state this analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r3.anchor: وقال الخفاجي إن جعل الشرطية في موضع المفعول والجملة الإستفهامية في موقع جواب الشرط

ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ's reading shifts the pronouns: the worshipper is guided and commands piety, while the forbidding man denies and turns away, making the contrast astonishing; the answer is understood as How astonishing.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r4.anchor: وقيل الضميران في أن كان وأمر للعبد المصلي والضمائر في كذب وتولي ويعلم للذي ينهى وحاصل المعنى على ما قال الفراء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r5.claim: On that parse, raʾayta may mean knowing or seeing; the first answer is omitted, and aw may mean and rather than divide two alternatives.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r5.anchor: والظاهر أن جواب الشرط عليه محذوف وهو فما أعجب من ذا بقرينة أرأيت

ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r6.claim: One view shifts the question's addressee from Abu Jahl to the Prophet, like a judge addressing opposing litigants.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r6.anchor: وقيل الخطاب في أرأيت الثانية للكافر وفي الثانية للنبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم فهو عز وجل كالحاكم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r7.claim: Piety is separately mentioned because forbidding prayer may also forbid its spoken invitation; prayer as enacted example is stronger than speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r7.anchor: ولعل ذكر الأمر بالتقوى في الجملة الثانية لأن النهي على ما قيل كان عن الصلاة والأمر بها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r8.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r8.claim: Another explanation says the first prohibition occurs while the worshipper is praying, a state that includes both worship and inviting others; al-Rāzī allows the address throughout to be the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p185/r8.anchor: وقيل المذكور أولا ليس النهي عن الصلاة بل النهي حين الصلاة وهو محتمل أن يكون لها أو لغيرها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r1.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r1.claim: The hypothetical asks whether the forbidding man, as a wealthy and intelligent person, should have chosen guidance and piety for himself; this would have been better than disbelief and preventing worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r1.anchor: أرأيت إن صار على الهدى واشتغل بأمر نفسه أما كان يليق به ذلك إذ هو رجل عاقل ذو ثروة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r2.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r2.claim: The passage laments that he forfeited lofty ranks and settled for base ones.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r2.anchor: كأنه تعالى يقول تلهف عليه كيف فوت على نفسه المراتب العلية وقنع بالمراتب الردية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r3.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r3.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn reads the first question as proof of the tyrant's overreach, the second as reproach for missing benefit, and the third as reproach for earning punishment; the last clause threatens him after the contrast of lost good and acquired evil.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r3.anchor: اعتبر عصام الدين هذه الجملة توبيخا على تفويت ما ينفع وما بعدها توبيخا على كسب ما يضر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r4.claim: Although revealed about Abu Jahl, the warning applies to anyone who prevents prayer; prohibiting prayer in a usurped place or disliked time targets its accompanying circumstance, not prayer itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r4.anchor: لكن كل من نهى عن الصلاة ومنع منها فهو شريكه في الوعيد ولا يلزم على ذلك المنع عن النهي عن الصلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r5.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r5.claim: ʿAlī reportedly declined to stop people praying before the Eid prayer, fearing the warning; instead he told them he had not seen the Messenger do it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r5.anchor: فروي عن أمير المؤمنين كرم الله تعالى وجهه أنه رأى في المصلى أقواما يصلون قبل صلاة العيد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r6.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa similarly avoided direct prohibition: when Abū Yūsuf asked what a worshipper should say after bowing, he prescribed the established response and prostration rather than expressly forbidding it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r6.anchor: وقد سلك نحو هذا المسلك أبو حنيفة عليه الرحمة فقد روي أن أبا يوسف قال له

ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r7.claim: The warning extends by analogy to prohibiting other forms of worship, whether the interference is verbal or practical, including distracting someone from worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p186/r7.anchor: ويقاس على النهي عن الصلاة النهي عن غيرها من أنواع العبادة ولا فرق بين النهي القالي والنهي الحالي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r11.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r11.claim: Abu Jahl threatened to trample the Prophet while praying, but recoiled from a trench of fire, terror, and wings; the Prophet said angels would seize him limb by limb. The report is uncertain about whether the revelation was in Abu Hurayra's narration or another source.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r11.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال أبو جهل: هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r5.claim: Does he not know means Abu Jahl knows God sees his actions and will punish him for them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r5.anchor: ألم يعلم} يعني أبا جهل، {بأن الله يرى} ذلك فيجازيه به

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r6.claim: Kalla means that Abu Jahl does not know this.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r6.anchor: كلا} لا يعلم ذلك، {لئن لم ينته}

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r3.claim: The repeated أَرَأَيْتَ construction has the same grammatical function; its conditional is the second object, and its answer is omitted but supplied by the later condition. God sees the person's guidance and error.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r3.anchor: أرأيت تكرير للأول وكذا الذي في قوله:

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r4.claim: One reading asks whether the forbidding person is himself guided and commands piety as he understands idol worship, or whether he is a denier who turns from truth; God sees all his states.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r4.anchor: إن كان ذلك الناهي على هدى فيما ينهى عنه، أو آمرا { بالتقوى }

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.claim: A report promises the reciter a reward as though he had recited the entire set of shorter suras.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.anchor: من قرأ سورة العلق أعطي من الأجر كأنما قرأ المفصل كله

BINTSHATI:v2p27/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r1.claim: Continuing al-Razi’s first solution, the rest of the surah came later about Abu Jahl, and the Prophet was directed to place these verses at its beginning.
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r1.anchor: نزلت البقية في أبي جهل بن هشام، وأمر الرسول - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بضمها إلى أول السورة

BINTSHATI:v2p27/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r2.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r2.claim: Al-Razi’s second solution reads الإنسان generically: despite creation and blessings, people transgress, forget their return, and forbid worship when they should follow guidance and enjoin piety.
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r2.anchor: أن تحمل الآيات على عموم لفظها في الظاهر، وهو أن الإنسان، جملة الإنسان، خلقه الله من علق

BINTSHATI:v2p27/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r3.claim: Both explanations are possible; the sequence suggests the passage followed public preaching and prayer, while a specific occasion does not prevent the wording from applying generally.
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r3.anchor: وكلا الوجهين جائز. فسياق الآيات في السورة، يشعر بأنها نزلت بعد أن أبلغ المصطفى رسالة ربه

BINTSHATI:v2p27/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari makes the conditional clause in verse 13 the second object of arayta in verse 9, treats arayta before the condition as extra, and takes verse 14 as the condition’s answer.
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r4.anchor: ذهب الزمخشري في (الكشاف) إلى أن الجملة الشرطية في {أَرَأَيْتَ إِنْ كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى}

BINTSHATI:v2p27/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r5.claim: She objects that this analysis inserts an extra arayta into the flow and leaves an interrogative response unprefixed by fa, contrary to the grammarians’ rule.
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r5.anchor: تبدو فيه {أَرَأَيْتَ} في الجملة الشرطية مقحمة على السياق، تمت للزمخشري تسوية الصنعة

BINTSHATI:v2p28/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r1.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects al-Zamakhshari’s analysis, holding that arayta’s second object must be an interrogative sentence, a construction frequent in the Quran.
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r1.anchor: وكذلك رفض مذهب الزمخشري في جعل {أَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَرَى} جواباً لشرط {إِنْ كَذَّبَ}

BINTSHATI:v2p28/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r2.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r2.claim: Abu Hayyan says an interrogative cannot answer a condition without fa except under poetic necessity, so he rejects al-Zamakhshari’s proposed answer.
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r2.anchor: بل نصوا على وجوب الفاء في كل ما اقتضى طلباً بوجه ما، ولا يجوز حذفها إلا في ضرورة شعرية

BINTSHATI:v2p28/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r3.claim: She argues that Quranic interrogative arayta usually omits its second object and directs attention instead to the lesson or warning; she cites several Meccan examples.
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r3.anchor: وإنما يستغنى عن هذا المفعول، بتقرير يلفت إلى موضع العبرة والنذير

BINTSHATI:v2p29/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p29/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p29/r2.claim: The repeated arayta in this passage is a stylistic prompt to see and reflect on the warning; it need not take an explicit or inferred second object.
BINTSHATI:v2p29/r2.anchor: فلفتت إلى ما هو جدير بالرؤية والبصر والتدبر، وأغنت عما تعلق به النجاة من مفعول ثان

BINTSHATI:v2p29/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p29/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p29/r3.claim: Verse 14 itself supplies the focal lesson in place of an assumed conditional answer: knowing that God sees is the needed warning, without a hidden answer clause.
BINTSHATI:v2p29/r3.anchor: لتكون آية {أَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَرَى} هو موضع العبرة والبصر والتنبيه

BINTSHATI:v2p30/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p30/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p30/r1.claim: Other Quranic conditional questions are followed by interrogatives without fa, including examples in al-Anam, al-Qasas, and Hud.
BINTSHATI:v2p30/r1.anchor: والاستفهام فيها في موضع حواب الشرط، غير مقترن بالفاء

BINTSHATI:v2p30/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p30/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p30/r3.claim: She urges readers to notice Quranic stylistic patterns even when they depart from school grammar and rhetoric, rather than forcing them into technical rules by conjecture.
BINTSHATI:v2p30/r3.anchor: فيشغلنا عن البيان العالى، تسوية الصنعة النحوية أو البلاغية، بالتأويل فيه والتقدير

BIQAI-FULL:v8p485/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p485/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p485/r1.claim: The question supplies the second object of raʾayta: does the forbiddener not know that God sees, with absolute knowledge and sight of every knowable and visible thing?
BIQAI-FULL:v8p485/r1.anchor: ذاكرا مفعول ( أرءيت ) الثاني وهو لا يكون إلا جملة استفهامية

BIQAI-FULL:v8p485/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p485/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p485/r2.claim: One who sees all is able to destroy the misguiding wrongdoer and help whoever obeys Him against enemies; the rebuke uses what the opponents themselves acknowledge, exposing the contradiction in their hostility to the Prophet.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p485/r2.anchor: فهو يعلم كل معلوم ويبصر كل مبصر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p485/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p485/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p485/r5.claim: The author regards the forbiddener's conduct as irrational toward himself and his fellow human beings, despite God's watching and control over him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p485/r5.anchor: من حالته البعيدة عن العقل مع نفسه ومع نفسه ومع أبناء جنسه

DURR-FULL:v8p565/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r3.claim: He says the passage was revealed about Abu Jahl's threat to trample Muhammad; the guided one is Muhammad, the denier is Abu Jahl, his assembly is his clan, and ‘zabaniya’ means police in Arabic.
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى} قال: نزلت في عدو الله أبي جهل

BURHAN:v3p83/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p83/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p83/r2.claim: The bāʾ can be added to an object even though the verb takes it directly, as in “do not cast yourselves,” “shake the trunk,” and “does he not know that God sees?”
BURHAN:v3p83/r2.anchor: وفي المفعول نحو ﴿ ولا تلقوا بأيديكم إلى التهلكة ﴾

BURHAN:v4p154/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p154/r1.speaker: سيبويه
BURHAN:v4p154/r1.claim: Sībawayh says أرأيت cannot be left without its required object like علمت; in a question such as أرأيت زيدا أبو من هو, accusative is required.
BURHAN:v4p154/r1.anchor: قال سيبويه لا يجوز الغاء ارايت كما يلغى علمت

BURHAN:v4p154/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p154/r2.speaker: السهيلي
BURHAN:v4p154/r2.claim: Al-Suhaylī says the Qur'an appears to contradict Sībawayh: in أرأيت إن كذب وتولى ألم يعلم, the following question seems to cancel أرأيت.
BURHAN:v4p154/r2.anchor: قال السهيلي وظاهر القرآن يقتضي خلاف قوله وذلك انها في القرآن ملغاة

BURHAN:v4p154/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p154/r3.speaker: السهيلي
BURHAN:v4p154/r3.claim: Al-Suhaylī also cites أرأيتم and أرأيتكم in al-Anʿām, where questions follow, including هل يهلك إلا القوم الظالمون.
BURHAN:v4p154/r3.anchor: وكذلك ارايتم و ارايتكم في الانعام والاستفهام واقع بعدها نحو ﴿ هل يهلك إلا القوم الظالمون ﴾

BURHAN:v4p154/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p154/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p154/r4.claim: The author reconciles the analyses: Sībawayh is right when a question directly follows أرأيت and no other object is present; the Qur'anic cases have a condition pointing to an omitted object, while the question begins a new utterance.
BURHAN:v4p154/r4.anchor: لكن الذي قال سيبويه صحيح لكن اذا ولى الاستفهام ارايت ولم يكن لها مفعول سوى الجملة

ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains that God observes the forbider’s guidance or error and recompenses him accordingly; the statement is a threat.
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r10.anchor: ويطلع على أحواله من هداة وضلالة ، فيجازيه على حسب ذلك ، وهذا وعيد

ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r11.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r11.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reads the servant as guided and enjoining piety, and the forbider as denying and turning away; Abū Jahl is rebuked for ignoring God’s sight. Prayer reforms the Prophet himself and enjoining piety reforms others, both of which troubled Abū Jahl.
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r11.anchor: قال الفراء : المعنى { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } ، وهو على الهدى وأمر بالتقوى ، والناهي مكذب متول عن الذكر

ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r12.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this completes the rebuke and threat, fitting each of the three preceding formulations; the concise threat suffices for all.
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : { ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى } : إكمال التوبيخ والوعيد بحسب التوفيقات الثلاثة يصلح مع كل واحد منها

ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r14.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r14.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats “did he not know?” as the omitted conditional answer, supplied by the second condition; he argues it may answer without fāʾ, by analogy with two interrogative examples.
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r14.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : فإن قلت : ما متعلق { أرأيت } ؟ قلت : { الذي ينهى } مع الجملة الشرطية

ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r19.speaker: author

ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r19.anchor: وأما تجويز الزمخشري وقوع جملة الاستفهام جواباً للشرط بغير فاء ، فلا أعلم أحداً أجازه ، بل نصوا على وجوب الفاء

ALUSI:96:10/r32.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r32.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r32.claim: First the passage warns generally against forbidding prayer: does the prohibiter not know God sees and will punish him?
ALUSI:96:10/r32.anchor: فشنع سبحانه على الناهي أولاً بنهيه عن الصلاة وأوعد عليه مطلقاً

ALUSI:96:10/r33.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r33.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r33.claim: Next it warns him even on the supposition that he claims guidance in forbidding prayer or claims to command piety.
ALUSI:96:10/r33.anchor: وشنع سبحانه عليه ثانياً بنهيه عن ذلك وأوعده عليه أيضاً على تقدير أنه على زعمه على هدى ورشد

ALUSI:96:10/r34.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r34.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r34.claim: Finally it warns him on the actual premise that he denies prayer’s truth and turns away from it.
ALUSI:96:10/r34.anchor: وشنع جل شأنه عليه ثالثاً بذلك وأوعده عليه أيضاً على تقدير أنه في نفس الأمر

ALUSI:96:10/r36.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r36.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI:96:10/r36.claim: The majority read the first condition as a supposedly righteous course in forbidding worship of God or commanding piety while calling to idols, and the next as the prohibiter’s actual denial and turning away.
ALUSI:96:10/r36.anchor: والجمهور على عدم تقييد ما في حيز الشرطيتين بما ذكرنا حيث قالوا إن كان على طريقة سديدة

ALUSI:96:10/r39.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r39.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:10/r39.claim: In that parsing, the final question is unjoined to signal its independent actual occurrence and ensuing threat; the earlier condition only broadens the case and refers to the later answer.
ALUSI:96:10/r39.anchor: ولم تعطف الأخيرة على ما قبلها للإيذان باستقلالها بالوقوع في نفس الأمر

ALUSI:96:10/r40.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r40.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:10/r40.claim: Another analysis takes all three questions as inward seeing: the first conditional’s answer is omitted in favor of the second’s, while the third question independently opposes the first condition.
ALUSI:96:10/r40.anchor: وقيل إن أرأيت في الجمل الثلاث من الرؤية القلبية والمفعول الأول للأولى الموصول

ALUSI:96:10/r48.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r48.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI:96:10/r48.claim: Al-Farrāʾ’s reading makes the worshipper the subject of the second condition and the prohibiter the subject of the third: the worshipper is guided and commands piety, while the prohibiter denies and turns away—how astonishing.
ALUSI:96:10/r48.anchor: وحاصل المعنى على ما قال الفراء أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً يصلي والمنهي على الهدى وأمر بالتقوى

ALUSI:96:10/r50.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r50.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:10/r50.claim: One view splits the address between the disbeliever and the Messenger, like a judge speaking to opposing litigants.
ALUSI:96:10/r50.anchor: وقيل الخطاب في أرأيت الثانية للكافر وفي الثانية للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI:96:10/r54.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r54.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:96:10/r54.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn reads 96:9–10 as exposing tyranny when a person feels self-sufficient, 96:11–12 as rebuking lost guidance and piety, and 96:13–14 as rebuking earned punishment and distance from God.
ALUSI:96:10/r54.anchor: واعتبر عصام الدين هذه الجملة توبيخاً على تفويت ما ينفع وما بعدها توبيخاً على كسب ما يضر

ALUSI:96:10/r55.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r55.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r55.claim: Al-Ālūsī distances himself from ʿIṣām al-Dīn’s elaboration, inviting reflection and leaving the matter to God’s intended meaning.
ALUSI:96:10/r55.anchor: وهو كما ترى فتأمل جميع ما تقدم والله تعالى بمراده أعلم

ALUSI:96:12/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:12/r23.claim: Al-Ālūsī reads three escalating reproaches: first for forbidding prayer without regard to the forbidder’s state, then on the state he claims, and finally on his actual denial and turning away, each ending in divine threat.
ALUSI:96:12/r23.anchor: والحاصل أنه تعالى شنع وأوعد على النهي عن الصلاة بدون تعرض لحال الناهي الزعمي أو الحقيقي ثم شنع وأوعد جل وعلا عليه مع التعرض لحاله الزعمي

ALUSI:96:12/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r25.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:96:12/r25.claim: One parsing makes the first question visual and the next two intellectual; the conditional clauses fill the second-object position, while the uncoordinated final clause stresses its occurrence and threat.
ALUSI:96:12/r25.anchor: وقيل إن الرؤية في الجملة الأولى بصرية فلا تحتاج إلى مفعول ثان وفي الثانية والثالثة قلبية

ALUSI:96:12/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r26.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:96:12/r26.claim: A further parsing takes all three questions as intellectual: the first relative clause is its first object, the first conditional supplies its second object through an omitted answer, and the third question stands independently.
ALUSI:96:12/r26.anchor: وقيل إن أرأيت في الجمل الثلاث من الرؤية القلبية والمفعول الأول للأولى الموصول ومفعولها الثاني الجملة الشرطية الأولى بجوابها المحذوف

ALUSI:96:12/r27.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r27.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:96:12/r27.claim: Another account treats the second and third arayta as repetitions of the first; both conditions occupy its second-object position, ألم يعلم answers the second, and the first answer is omitted as understood.
ALUSI:96:12/r27.anchor: وقيل أرأيت في الجملتين الثانية والثالثة تكرار للأولى والشرطيتان بجوابهما سادتان مسد المفعول الثاني للأولى

ALUSI:96:12/r28.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r28.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI:96:12/r28.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows an interrogative clause to answer a conditional without fa, citing 6:47; Abū Ḥayyān says a request clause requires fa except in poetic or necessary usage.
ALUSI:96:12/r28.anchor: وإن صرح له الزمخشري في كشافه وارتضاه الرضي واستشهد له بقوله تعالى : { قل أرأيتم

ALUSI:96:12/r34.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r34.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI:96:12/r34.claim: Al-Farrāʾ assigns كان and أمر to the praying servant, but كذب and تولى and يعلم to the forbidder: the servant is guided and enjoins piety while the forbidder denies and turns away.
ALUSI:96:12/r34.anchor: وقيل الضميران في أن كان وأمر للعبد المصلي والضمائر في كذب وتولى ويعلم للذي ينهى وحاصل المعنى على ما قال الفراء

ALUSI:96:12/r35.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r35.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:96:12/r35.claim: One view alternates addresses, asking the unbeliever whether he would forbid prayer that guides and calls to piety, then asking the Prophet whether the denier knows God sees him.
ALUSI:96:12/r35.anchor: وقيل الخطاب في أرأيت الثانية للكافر وفي الثانية للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فهو عز وجل كالحاكم الذي حضر الخصمان

ALUSI:96:12/r39.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r39.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:96:12/r39.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn reads 96:9 as exposing tyranny born of self-sufficiency, 96:11 as reproaching lost guidance and piety, 96:13 as reproaching earned punishment and distance from God, and 96:14 as the threat after both reproaches.
ALUSI:96:12/r39.anchor: واعتبر عصام الدين هذه الجملة توبيخاً على تفويت ما ينفع وما بعدها توبيخاً على كسب ما يضر

ALUSI:96:13/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r1.claim: The passage from 96:9 onward recounts some consequences of human tyranny and threatens the one who prevents prayer.
ALUSI:96:13/r1.anchor: ذكر لبعض آثار الطغيان ووعيد عليها

ALUSI:96:13/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r17.claim: In the principal parse, the first raʾayta takes the relative clause as its first object; the second and third have an omitted first object referring back, and the third’s second object is “does he not know that God sees?”
ALUSI:96:13/r17.anchor: والمفعول الأول للأول الموصول وللثاني والثالث محذوف وهو ضمير يعود عليه

ALUSI:96:13/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r19.claim: The answers to both conditional clauses are omitted, with 96:14 indicating them; another parse takes raʾayta itself to point to the answer soon to be stated.
ALUSI:96:13/r19.anchor: وجواب الشرط في الجملتين محذوف لدلالة ألم يعلم عليه

ALUSI:96:13/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r25.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r25.claim: The passage escalates: first it condemns forbidding prayer without regard to the forbidding person’s supposed status, then condemns it if he claims guidance, then if he actually denies prayer’s truth and turns away.
ALUSI:96:13/r25.anchor: والحاصل أنه تعالى شنع وأوعد على النهي عن الصلاة بدون تعرض لحال الناهي الزعمي أو الحقيقي

ALUSI:96:13/r27.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r27.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI:96:13/r27.claim: For the majority, the conditional form feigns latitude and taunts: there can be no guidance in forbidding worship of God and ordering idol worship, while the denier plainly is astray; both conditions return to one point.
ALUSI:96:13/r27.anchor: إذ لا يكون في النهي عن عبادته تعالى والأمر بعبادة الأصنام هدى البتة

ALUSI:96:13/r28.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r28.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:13/r28.claim: One parse makes the first raʾayta visual, needing no second object, and the second and third cognitive, with their conditional clauses and answers filling the second-object position.
ALUSI:96:13/r28.anchor: وقيل إن الرؤية في الجملة الأولى بصرية فلا تحتاج إلى مفعول ثان

ALUSI:96:13/r29.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r29.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:13/r29.claim: Another parse treats all three as cognitive: the first takes the relative clause as object one, its condition as object two, and the third omits object one while explicitly supplying the threatening answer.
ALUSI:96:13/r29.anchor: وقيل إن أرأيت في الجمل الثلاث من الرؤية القلبية والمفعول الأول للأولى الموصول

ALUSI:96:13/r30.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r30.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:13/r30.claim: In that parse, the final clause is unjoined to reinforce the rebuke and signal the condition’s truth; stating its answer makes the threat explicit, while the first conditional’s answer is understood from the second.
ALUSI:96:13/r30.anchor: وفي الإتيان بالجملة الأخيرة من دون العطف ترشيح للكلام المبكت وتنبيه على حقية الشرط

ALUSI:96:13/r31.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r31.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:13/r31.claim: A further parse makes the second and third raʾayta repetitions of the first; both conditionals fill its second-object slot, 96:14 answers the second, and the first answer is omitted by analogy.
ALUSI:96:13/r31.anchor: وقيل أرأيت في الجملتين الثانية والثالثة تكرار للأولى

ALUSI:96:13/r32.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r32.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:96:13/r32.claim: Abū Ḥayyān objects that an interrogative sentence cannot answer a conditional without faʾ; he says grammarians require it whenever the answer expresses a request, except in poetic necessity.
ALUSI:96:13/r32.anchor: وقال أبو حيان إن وقوع جملة الاستفهام جواباً للشرط بغير فاء لا أعلم أحد أجازه

ALUSI:96:13/r36.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r36.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI:96:13/r36.claim: Al-Farrāʾ assigns “was” and “commanded” to the praying servant, but “denied,” “turned away,” and “knows” to the prohibitor; the implied conclusion is how astonishing the case is.
ALUSI:96:13/r36.anchor: وحاصل المعنى على ما قال الفراء أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً يصلي والمنهي على الهدى

ALUSI:96:13/r37.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r37.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:13/r37.claim: Another proposal shifts the second question’s addressee to the disbeliever and the third’s to the Prophet, like a judge addressing two litigants; its “or” is division equivalent to “and.”
ALUSI:96:13/r37.anchor: فهو عز وجل كالحاكم الذي حضر الخصمان يخاطب هذا مرة والآخر أخرى

ALUSI:96:13/r41.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r41.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI:96:13/r41.claim: The Imam reads the condition as asking whether a sensible, wealthy man would not do better to seek guidance and command piety than disbelieve and prohibit worship; God laments his forfeiture of high ranks for low ones.
ALUSI:96:13/r41.anchor: وجوز الإمام كون الخطاب في الكل له عليه الصلاة والسلام وقال في بيان معنى

ALUSI:96:13/r42.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r42.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:96:13/r42.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn reads 96:9 as tyranny born of self-sufficiency, 96:11–12 as rebuke for forfeiting guidance and piety, and 96:13 as rebuke for earning punishment and distance from God; 96:14 is a severe threat.
ALUSI:96:13/r42.anchor: واعتبر عصام الدين هذه الجملة توبيخاً على تفويت ما ينفع وما بعدها توبيخاً على كسب ما يضر

ALUSI:96:13/r45.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r45.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:96:13/r45.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn takes the final question as rebuke for earned harm: denial and turning away merit punishment and distance from the Lord, followed by a severe threat.
ALUSI:96:13/r45.anchor: عصام الدين هذه الجملة توبيخاً على تفويت ما ينفع وما بعدها توبيخاً على كسب ما يضر

ALUSI:96:14/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI:96:14/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says commentators agree that the praying servant is the Messenger and the one forbidding him is Abū Jahl.
ALUSI:96:14/r1.anchor: لم يختلف المفسرون كما قال ابن عطية في أن العبد المصلي هو رسول الله

ALUSI:96:14/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI:96:14/r2.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that Abū Jahl swore by al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā to trample the Prophet while he prayed; he recoiled from a fiery trench and wings, and the passage through the sūra was then revealed.
ALUSI:96:14/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن أبا جهل حلف باللات والعزى لئن رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI:96:14/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r3.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI:96:14/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the forbidder as Umayya b. Khalaf and the praying servant as Salmān; al-Ālūsī rejects this as unlikely because Salmān became Muslim in Medina while the sūra is Meccan.
ALUSI:96:14/r3.anchor: وقول الحسن هو أمية بن خلف كان ينهى سلمان عن الصلاة لا يكاد يصح

ALUSI:96:14/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:14/r4.claim: Although the occasion concerns Abū Jahl, the warning applies to anyone who prevents prayer; if the Umayya report is true, the general warning includes him too.
ALUSI:96:14/r4.anchor: نعم حكم الآية عام فإن كان ما حكي عن أمية واقعاً فحكمها شامل له

ALUSI:96:14/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:96:14/r5.claim: Abū Ḥayyān reports that the prayer was Ẓuhr and also that it was the first congregational prayer, with the Prophet, Abū Bakr, and ʿAlī.
ALUSI:96:14/r5.anchor: حكى أبو حيان صلاة الظهر وحكي أيضاً أنها كانت تصلي جماعة وهي أول جماعة أقيمت

ALUSI:96:14/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:96:14/r6.claim: Abū Ḥayyān also relates that Abū Ṭālib passed with Jaʿfar, told him to pray beside his cousin, and left delighted, composing praise and an appeal to protect the Prophet.
ALUSI:96:14/r6.anchor: فمر أبو طالب ومعه ابنه جعفر فقال له يا بني صل جناح ابن عمك وانصرف مسروراً

ALUSI:96:14/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:14/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī questions the Abū Ṭālib story: prayer became obligatory on the Miʿrāj, which Ibn Ḥazm dates one year before the Hijra, Ibn Fāris one year and three months, and al-Suddī one year and five months; Abū Ṭālib died earlier.
ALUSI:96:14/r7.anchor: لأن الصلاة فرضت ليلة الإسراء بلا خلاف وادعى ابن حزم الإجماع على أنه كان قبل الهجرة بسنة

ALUSI:96:14/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r8.speaker: الزهري
ALUSI:96:14/r8.claim: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ reports from al-Zuhrī, with Nawawī and Qurṭubī favoring it, that the Miʿrāj occurred five years after the prophetic commission; objections to this chronology are noted.
ALUSI:96:14/r8.anchor: حكى القاضي عياض عن الزهري ورجحه النووي والقرطبي أن الإسراء كان بعد البعث بخمس سنين

ALUSI:96:14/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:14/r9.claim: One explanation takes the forbidding as physical prevention; the wording hints at the tyrant's inability to do more than that.
ALUSI:96:14/r9.anchor: والنهي قيل بمعنى المنع وعبر به إشارة إلى عدم اقتدار اللعين على غير ذلك

ALUSI:96:14/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:96:14/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Abū Jahl verbally warned the Prophet, asking twice whether he had not forbidden him; al-Tirmidhī authenticated this report, also transmitted by Aḥmad and others.
ALUSI:96:14/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال «كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي فجاء أبو جهل

ALUSI:96:14/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:14/r11.claim: The future form evokes the past scene vividly because it is strange and remarkable.
ALUSI:96:14/r11.anchor: والتعبير بما يفيد الاستقبال لاستحضار الصورة الماضية لنوع غرابة

ALUSI:96:14/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:14/r12.claim: Here raʾayta means inform me: since seeing leads to knowledge, asking about seeing stands for asking about its object; scholars differ on whether this usage works with visual and intellectual seeing.
ALUSI:96:14/r12.anchor: والمراد من أرأيت أخبرني فإن الرؤية لما كانت سبباً للعلم أجري الاستفهام عنها مجرى الاستخبار

ALUSI:96:14/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:14/r13.claim: In one parsing, the first raʾayta has the relative clause as its first object, while the second and third omit a returning pronoun or demonstrative; the third object's second complement is this verse, with analogous omissions in the first two.
ALUSI:96:14/r13.anchor: والمفعول الأول للأول الموصول وللثاني والثالث محذوف وهو ضمير يعود عليه

ALUSI:96:14/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:14/r14.claim: This is not syntactic tanāzuʿ: clauses cannot be elided as objects here; it is semantic demand, with deletion outside tanāzuʿ.
ALUSI:96:14/r14.anchor: وليس ذلك من التنازع لأن الجمل لا يصح إضمارها وإنما هو من الطلب المعنوي

ALUSI:96:14/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:14/r15.claim: The two conditional apodoses are omitted and supplied by the indication of this verse; another analysis makes them indicated by raʾayta and estimates them according to the syntax.
ALUSI:96:14/r15.anchor: وجواب الشرط في الجملتين محذوف لدلالة ألم يعلم عليه ويقدر حسبما تقتضيه الصناعة

ALUSI:96:14/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:14/r16.claim: Some say the first raʾayta is visual and needs no second object, while the second and third are cognitive; the conditional clauses with their answers fill the latter's second-object position.
ALUSI:96:14/r16.anchor: وقيل إن الرؤية في الجملة الأولى بصرية فلا تحتاج إلى مفعول ثان

ALUSI:96:14/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:14/r17.claim: Al-Ālūsī's staged reading makes the passage rebuke and threaten the forbidding first without considering his claimed or actual state, then on his claimed guidance, then on his actual denial and turning away.
ALUSI:96:14/r17.anchor: والحاصل أنه تعالى شنع وأوعد على النهي عن الصلاة بدون تعرض لحال الناهي الزعمي أو الحقيقي

ALUSI:96:14/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r18.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI:96:14/r18.claim: The majority do not restrict the two conditions: the first sarcastically grants the forbidder's claimed guidance or piety in promoting idolatry, and the second grants his evident denial and turning away; both lead to the same rebuke.
ALUSI:96:14/r18.anchor: والجمهور على عدم تقييد ما في حيز الشرطيتين بما ذكرنا

ALUSI:96:14/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:14/r19.claim: Another analysis takes all three raʾayta as cognitive; the first condition with its omitted answer fills the second object, the second repeats the first, and the final condition stands independently, its answer made explicit to sharpen the threat.
ALUSI:96:14/r19.anchor: وقيل إن أرأيت في الجمل الثلاث من الرؤية القلبية والمفعول الأول للأولى الموصول

ALUSI:96:14/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:14/r20.claim: A further parsing makes the second and third raʾayta repetitions, with both conditionals filling the first one's second object; the final verse answers the second condition and the first answer is understood from it.
ALUSI:96:14/r20.anchor: وقيل أرأيت في الجملتين الثانية والثالثة تكرار للأولى والشرطيتان بجوابهما سادتان مسد المفعول الثاني للأولى

ALUSI:96:14/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r21.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI:96:14/r21.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows an interrogative as a conditional answer without faʾ, and al-Raḍī approves; the cited example is 6:47, but the construction is challenged.
ALUSI:96:14/r21.anchor: وإن صرح له الزمخشري في كشافه وارتضاه الرضي واستشهد له بقوله تعالى

ALUSI:96:14/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r22.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:96:14/r22.claim: Abū Ḥayyān objects that no grammarian he knows permits an interrogative apodosis without faʾ; request-like clauses require it, except by poetic necessity.
ALUSI:96:14/r22.anchor: وقال أبو حيان إن وقوع جملة الاستفهام جواباً للشرط بغير فاء لا أعلم أحد أجازه

ALUSI:96:14/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r23.speaker: الدماميني
ALUSI:96:14/r23.claim: Al-Damāmīnī likewise finds it difficult to treat hal yahliku in 6:47 as the conditional answer because the required faʾ is absent.
ALUSI:96:14/r23.anchor: وقال الدماميني في شرح التسهيل إن جعل هل يهلك جزاء مشكل لعدم اقترانه بالفاء

ALUSI:96:14/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r24.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:96:14/r24.claim: A further objection says raʾayta's second object must be an interrogative or oath clause, not a conditional clause.
ALUSI:96:14/r24.anchor: بأن مفعولها الثاني لا يكون إلا جملة استفهامية كمانص عليه أبو حيان وجماعة أو قسمية

ALUSI:96:14/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r25.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI:96:14/r25.claim: Al-Khafājī replies that the conditional and interrogative clauses may occupy the object and answer positions literally, or by implication as though they filled those positions; al-Raḍī and al-Damāmīnī state this too.
ALUSI:96:14/r25.anchor: وقال الخفاجي إن جعل الشرطية في موقع المفعول والجملة الاستفهامية في موقع جواب الشرط

ALUSI:96:14/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r26.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:14/r26.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the categorical claim that raʾayta's second object must only be interrogative, since that conflicts with what they report as Sībawayh's preferred view.
ALUSI:96:14/r26.anchor: المفعول الثاني لا رأيت لا يكون إلا جملة استفهامية مخالف لما صرحوا بأنه مختار سيبويه

ALUSI:96:14/r27.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r27.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:14/r27.claim: Some grammarians address the whole passage to anyone fit to be addressed; another view makes it address humanity, as in the address at 96:8.
ALUSI:96:14/r27.anchor: والخطاب في الكل على ما اختاره جمع لكل من يصلح أن يكون مخاطباً

ALUSI:96:14/r28.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r28.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:14/r28.claim: Some take the indefinite ʿabdan as generic; another analysis treats it as magnifying the Prophet and intensifying the wonder at the prohibition.
ALUSI:96:14/r28.anchor: وتنوين { عبداً } على ما هو ظاهر كلام البعض للتنكير

ALUSI:96:14/r29.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r29.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:14/r29.claim: The clauses are separated to make each reproach and threat independently forceful: the prohibition, the claimed piety, and the actual denial receive successive attention.
ALUSI:96:14/r29.anchor: وفصل بين الجمل للاعتناء بأمر التشنيع والوعيد حيث أشعر أن كل جملة مقصودة على حيالها

ALUSI:96:14/r30.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r30.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI:96:14/r30.claim: Al-Farrāʾ assigns the first condition's pronouns to the praying servant and the later denial, turning away, and knowing to the forbidder; the omitted response conveys how astonishing the situation is.
ALUSI:96:14/r30.anchor: وحاصل المعنى على ما قال الفراء أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً يصلي والمنهي على الهدى

ALUSI:96:14/r31.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r31.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI:96:14/r31.claim: In al-Farrāʾ's analysis, the connective aw is divisive, or it may mean wāw; the response is omitted as an expression of astonishment, with this verse resuming the point.
ALUSI:96:14/r31.anchor: والظاهر أن جواب الشرط عليه محذوف وهو فما أعجب من ذا بقرينة أرأيت

ALUSI:96:14/r32.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r32.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:14/r32.claim: A view distributes the interrogatives between the disbeliever and the Prophet, likening God to a judge addressing both litigants in turn.
ALUSI:96:14/r32.anchor: وقيل الخطاب في أرأيت الثانية للكافر وفي الثانية للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI:96:14/r33.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r33.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:14/r33.claim: Mentioning enjoining piety in the second condition is apt because forbidding a thing commands its opposite; it was omitted from the first condition as redundant, while prayer is foregrounded because action is stronger than speech.
ALUSI:96:14/r33.anchor: ولعل ذكر الأمر بالتقوى في الجملة الثانية لأن النهي على ما قيل كان عن الصلاة

ALUSI:96:14/r34.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r34.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI:96:14/r34.claim: The Imam reads the hypothetical guidance as a rebuke: a rational, wealthy man would have done better to seek guidance and enjoin piety than to disbelieve and prevent God's worship; God laments his lost higher rank.
ALUSI:96:14/r34.anchor: إن صار على الهدى واشتغل بأمر نفسه أما كان يليق به ذلك إذ هو رجل عاقل

ALUSI:96:14/r35.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r35.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:96:14/r35.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn reads 96:9 as evidence of tyranny when a self-sufficient person exceeds ingratitude by forbidding the servant sent to stop it; 96:11 rebukes lost guidance, 96:13 acquired punishment, and 96:14 threatens after those rebukes.
ALUSI:96:14/r35.anchor: واعتبر عصام الدين هذه الجملة توبيخاً على تفويت ما ينفع وما بعدها توبيخاً على كسب ما يضر

ALUSI:96:14/r36.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r36.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:14/r36.claim: The warning covers every attempt to stop prayer, but forbidding prayer in a usurped place or disliked time is not included because the objection concerns a concomitant quality, not prayer itself.
ALUSI:96:14/r36.anchor: ولا يلزم على ذلك المنع عن النهي عن الصلاة في الدار المغصوبة والأوقات المكروهة

ALUSI:96:14/r37.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r37.speaker: علي
ALUSI:96:14/r37.claim: ʿAlī refrained from forbidding people praying before the Eid prayer, fearing this threat; another report says he preferred to tell them what he saw the Prophet do rather than forbid a worshipper.
ALUSI:96:14/r37.anchor: فروي عن أمير المؤمنين كرم الله تعالى وجهه أنه رأى في المصلي أقواماً يصلون قبل صلاة العيد

ALUSI:96:14/r38.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r38.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI:96:14/r38.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa similarly avoids an explicit prohibition: when Abū Yūsuf asks what to say on rising from bowing, he supplies the formula and directs prostration without saying not to do it.
ALUSI:96:14/r38.anchor: وقد سلك نحو هذا المسلك أبو حنيفة عليه الرحمة فقد روي أن أبا يوسف قال له

ALUSI:96:14/r39.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:14/r39.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:14/r39.claim: The warning extends by analogy to stopping other kinds of worship, whether by words or by distracting someone from worship; many people are afflicted by this.
ALUSI:96:14/r39.anchor: ويقاس على النهي عن الصلاة النهي عن غيرها من أنواع العبادة ولا فرق بين النهي القالي والنهي الحالي

BAGHAWI:96:14/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:14/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:96:14/r1.claim: The one addressed is Abu Jahl; God sees his action and will repay him for it.
BAGHAWI:96:14/r1.anchor: ألم يعلم } يعني أبا جهل ، { بأن الله يرى } ذلك فيجازيه به

BAYDAWI:96:13/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:13/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:13/r1.claim: The conditional is the second object of Have you considered; its answer is omitted and supplied by the answer to the second conditional, which serves as its counterpart.
BAYDAWI:96:13/r1.anchor: والشرطية مفعوله الثاني ، وجواب الشرط محذوف دل عليه جواب الشرط الثاني الواقع موقع القسيم له

BAYDAWI:96:13/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:13/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:13/r2.claim: He asks about the one forbidding a servant’s prayer: is the forbidding man guided or enjoining piety as he believes in idol worship, or denying truth and turning from right? God sees each one’s guidance and error.
BAYDAWI:96:13/r2.anchor: أو آمرا بالتقوى فيما يأمر به من عبادة الأوثان كما يعتقده ، أو إن كان على التكذيب للحق والتولي عن الصواب كما تقول

BAYDAWI:96:13/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:13/r4.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI:96:13/r4.claim: Another interpretation makes the second address speak to the unbeliever, as a judge addresses two litigants in turn: would he forbid prayer that guides and calls to God?
BAYDAWI:96:13/r4.anchor: وقيل : الخطاب في الثانية مع الكافر ، فإنه سبحانه وتعالى كالحاكم الذي حضره الخصمان : يخاطب هذا مرة

BAYDAWI:96:14/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:14/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:14/r1.claim: The conditional is the second object of Have you considered; its answer is omitted and supplied by the answer to the second conditional, which serves as its counterpart.
BAYDAWI:96:14/r1.anchor: والشرطية مفعوله الثاني ، وجواب الشرط محذوف دل عليه جواب الشرط الثاني الواقع موقع القسيم له

BAYDAWI:96:14/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:14/r2.speaker: author

BAYDAWI:96:14/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:14/r4.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI:96:14/r4.claim: Another interpretation makes the second address speak to the unbeliever, as a judge addresses two litigants in turn: would he forbid prayer that guides and calls to God?
BAYDAWI:96:14/r4.anchor: وقيل : الخطاب في الثانية مع الكافر ، فإنه سبحانه وتعالى كالحاكم الذي حضره الخصمان : يخاطب هذا مرة

BIQAI:96:14/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:14/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:14/r1.claim: This clause supplies the second object of araʾayta, which must be an interrogative sentence; the rebuke exposes the person's irrationality despite knowing he is monitored and powerless.
BIQAI:96:14/r1.anchor: الثاني وهو لا يكون إلا جملة استفهامية

BIQAI:96:14/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:14/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:14/r2.claim: God has unrestricted sight and knowledge: He knows everything knowable and sees everything visible, so He can punish those who misguide and support those who obey Him.
BIQAI:96:14/r2.anchor: له صفتا البصر والعلم على الإطلاق

BIQAI:96:14/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:14/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:14/r3.claim: The denial is framed as an interrogative because the opponents admit the truths being denied; their hostility to the Prophet entails denying them, an irreconcilable contradiction.
BIQAI:96:14/r3.anchor: من عداوة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI:96:14/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:14/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:14/r5.claim: On the ihtibāk reading, the omitted response is that God sees all that can be seen, prohibits what He dislikes, does not approve it, and will judge it; the person should assess actions by rational and revealed evidence.

IBNASHUR:96:14/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:14/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:14/r1.claim: On the preceding interpretation, the condition's implied answer is that God knows and will punish the denier; this independent question denies that he is ignorant, and the condition plus answer supply the second object of arāʾayta.
IBNASHUR:96:14/r1.anchor: وعلى قولهم يتعين تقدير جواب الشرط بما يدل عليه :  { ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى } والتقدير :  إن كذب وتولى فالله عالم به

IBNASHUR:96:14/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:14/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:14/r2.claim: God's seeing is a metonym for the threat of punishment; the question rebukes the offender for failing to know this and protect himself from its consequence.
IBNASHUR:96:14/r2.anchor: وكني بأن الله يرى عن الوعيد بالعقاب

IBNASHUR:96:14/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:14/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:14/r3.claim: Yaʿlam is used with the sense of being certain, which accounts for its construction with bi.
IBNASHUR:96:14/r3.anchor: وضمن فعل { يعلم } معنى يوقن فلذلك عدي بالباء

IBNASHUR:96:14/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:14/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:14/r4.claim: Arāʾayta is suspended from taking its object because the following clause contains an interrogative.
IBNASHUR:96:14/r4.anchor: وعلق فعل { أرأيت } هنا عن العمل لوجود الاستفهام في قوله :  { ألم يعلم }

IBNASHUR:96:14/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:14/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:14/r7.claim: The object of God's seeing is omitted to include every existent; divine seeing here means God's knowledge as it relates to perceptible things.
IBNASHUR:96:14/r7.anchor: وحذف مفعول { يرى } ليعمّ كل موجود ،  والمراد بالرؤية المسندة إلى الله تعالى تعلق علمه بالمحسوسات

IBNATIYYA:96:9/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:9/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:9/r2.claim: The three interrogative challenges are arranged in sequence; the closing question supplies their omitted, expansive completions and one concise threat suffices for all.
IBNATIYYA:96:9/r2.anchor: فجاء بها في نسق ، ثم جاء بالوعيد الكافي لجميعها اختصاراً واقتضاباً

IBNATIYYA:96:10/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:10/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:10/r2.claim: The three interrogative challenges are arranged in sequence; the closing question supplies their omitted, expansive completions and one concise threat suffices for all.
IBNATIYYA:96:10/r2.anchor: فجاء بها في نسق ، ثم جاء بالوعيد الكافي لجميعها اختصاراً واقتضاباً

IBNATIYYA:96:11/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:11/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:11/r2.claim: The three interrogative challenges are arranged in sequence; the closing question supplies their omitted, expansive completions and one concise threat suffices for all.

IBNATIYYA:96:12/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:12/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:12/r2.claim: The three interrogative challenges are arranged in sequence; the closing question supplies their omitted, expansive completions and one concise threat suffices for all.
