IBNATIYYA:96:13/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:13/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:13/r2.claim: The three interrogative challenges are arranged in sequence; the closing question supplies their omitted, expansive completions and one concise threat suffices for all.
IBNATIYYA:96:13/r2.anchor: فجاء بها في نسق ، ثم جاء بالوعيد الكافي لجميعها اختصاراً واقتضاباً

IBNATIYYA:96:13/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:13/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:13/r4.claim: God’s seeing means apprehending everyone’s deeds; He is exalted above bodily organs and any likeness to created things.
IBNATIYYA:96:13/r4.anchor: ونسب الرؤية إلى الله تعالى بمعنى يدرك أعمال الجميع بإدراك : سماه رؤية

IBNATIYYA:96:14/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:14/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:14/r1.claim: Arayta is an interrogative challenge and, unlike knowledge-based vision, does not take two objects.
IBNATIYYA:96:14/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { أرأيت } توقيف ، وهو فعل لا يتعدى إلى مفعولين على حد الرؤية

IBNATIYYA:96:14/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:14/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:14/r2.claim: The three interrogative challenges are arranged in sequence; the closing question supplies their omitted, expansive completions and one concise threat suffices for all.
IBNATIYYA:96:14/r2.anchor: فجاء بها في نسق ، ثم جاء بالوعيد الكافي لجميعها اختصاراً واقتضاباً

IBNKATHIR:96:9/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:9/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:9/r4.claim: The forbidding man ought to know that God sees him, hears his speech, and will recompense his deed fully.
IBNKATHIR:96:9/r4.anchor: أي : أما علم هذا الناهي لهذا المهتدي أن الله يراه ويسمع كلامه ، وسيجازيه على فعله أتم الجزاء

IBNKATHIR:96:10/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:10/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:10/r4.claim: The forbidding man ought to know that God sees him, hears his speech, and will recompense his deed fully.
IBNKATHIR:96:10/r4.anchor: أي : أما علم هذا الناهي لهذا المهتدي أن الله يراه ويسمع كلامه ، وسيجازيه على فعله أتم الجزاء

IBNKATHIR:96:11/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:11/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:11/r4.claim: The forbidding man should know that God sees him, hears his words, and will recompense him fully.
IBNKATHIR:96:11/r4.anchor: أن الله يراه ويسمع كلامه ، وسيجازيه على فعله أتم الجزاء

IBNKATHIR:96:12/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:12/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:12/r4.claim: The forbidding man should know that God sees him, hears his words, and will recompense him fully.
IBNKATHIR:96:12/r4.anchor: أن الله يراه ويسمع كلامه ، وسيجازيه على فعله أتم الجزاء

IBNKATHIR:96:14/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:14/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:14/r4.claim: The forbidding man should know that God sees him, hears his words, and will recompense him fully.
IBNKATHIR:96:14/r4.anchor: أن الله يراه ويسمع كلامه ، وسيجازيه على فعله أتم الجزاء

MAWARDI:96:14/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:14/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:14/r2.claim: One address asks Muhammad whether he knows that God sees Abu Jahl.
MAWARDI:96:14/r2.anchor: ألم تعلم يا محمد أن الله يرى أبا جهل

MAWARDI:96:14/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:14/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:14/r3.claim: The other address asks Abu Jahl whether he knows that God sees him.
MAWARDI:96:14/r3.anchor: ألم تعلم يا أبا جهل أن الله يراك

MAWARDI:96:14/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:14/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:14/r4.claim: God sees Abu Jahl's deeds and hears his words.

MAWARDI:96:14/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:14/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:14/r5.claim: God sees Muhammad praying when Abu Jahl forbids him to pray.
MAWARDI:96:14/r5.anchor: يراك في صلاتك حين نهاك أبو جهل عنها

MAWARDI:96:14/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:14/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:14/r6.claim: God sees Abu Jahl's intention to harm the Messenger and prevents him from reaching him.
MAWARDI:96:14/r6.anchor: يرى ما همّ به أبو جهل فلا يمكنه من رسوله

NASAFI:96:14/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:14/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:14/r1.claim: God observes the person's guidance or error and requites him according to his state; this is a threat.
NASAFI:96:14/r1.anchor: ويطلع على أحواله من هداه وضلاله فيجازيه على حسب حاله

NASAFI:96:14/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:14/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:14/r2.claim: “The one who forbids” and the conditional clause are the two objects of the first “Have you seen?”; its omitted answer is supplied from the second condition, while the repeated question adds emphasis.
NASAFI:96:14/r2.anchor: { الذى ينهى } مع الجملة الشرطية مفعولا { أَرَأَيْتَ }

QURTUBI:96:13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:13/r2.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI:96:13/r2.claim: Al-Farra connects the clauses: the forbidden servant may be guided and command piety while the forbidding man denies and turns from the Reminder; the sequence marvels at this, then reproaches Abu Jahl for not knowing God sees and knows his act.
QURTUBI:96:13/r2.anchor: وقال الفراء : المعنى " أرأيت الذي ينهى . عبدا إذا صلى " وهو على الهدى

QURTUBI:96:13/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:13/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:96:13/r3.claim: Another grammatical view makes each later أرأيت a substitute for the first, with ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى as the predicate.
QURTUBI:96:13/r3.anchor: وقيل : كل واحد من " أرأيت " بدل من الأول . و " ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى " الخبر .

QURTUBI:96:14/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:14/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:14/r1.claim: Abu Jahl denied God's Book and turned away from belief.
QURTUBI:96:14/r1.anchor: يعني أبا جهل كذب بكتاب الله عز وجل ، وأعرض عن الإيمان .
